chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ibn Faddal, from Abu Jameela, from Muhammad ibn Ali al-Halabi, who said:

I heard Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) saying: 'The differing of the Banu Abbas is from the inevitable, and the Call is from the inevitable, and the emergence of the Qa'im is from the inevitable.' I said: 'And how is the Call?' He (peace be upon him) said: 'A caller will call from the sky at the beginning of the day:
ai.seo_question: What is the significance of the Call from the sky regarding Ali and Uthman in Shia eschatology?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi highlights the inevitability of the Qa'im's emergence alongside a unique eschatological phenomenon: dual celestial calls announcing the victory of Ali and his Shias against that of Uthman and his followers. This contrast underscores the Shia theological view of historical reconciliation, where the rival factions' claims are resolved by divine decree at the end of time. The narration emphasizes the certainty (al-mahdum) of these events, reinforcing the authority of the Ahl al-Bayt in the final judgment.
